result: Jag1 trans-activated Notch1 very weakly compared to other ligand-receptor combinations, despite activating Notch2 at levels comparable to Dll1. This weak Jag1-Notch1 signaling was observed in both CHO-K1 and C2C12 cell lines, and Jag1 was properly trafficked to the cell surface.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly highlighted this as a key finding, noting 'Jag1 ligand expressing cells failed to activate Notch1 receptor although were capable of activating Notch2' and that 'The results with Jag1 are surprising also because it exhibits some of the strongest binding to plate bound ligands.' The observation was confirmed in a second cell line, which reviewers noted 'suggests they reflect fundamental properties of the ligands/receptors.'

result: Lfng modulated trans-activation in a ligand-class-dependent manner: it enhanced Delta-mediated trans-activation (especially Dll1-Notch1, 3-fold increase) and weakened Jagged-mediated trans-activation (especially Jag1, >2.5-fold decrease) for both Notch1 and Notch2 receptors.
evaluation: Reviewers noted that 'their transactivation results with most ligands on Notch1 and 2 in the presence or absence of Lfng were largely consistent with previous publications,' providing confidence in the assay system. The ligand-class correlation with Lfng response was not specifically questioned.

result: Cis-interactions were predominantly inhibitory, except for strong cis-activation of Notch2 by Dll1 and Dll4 at levels exceeding maximal trans-activation. Notch1 showed minimal cis-activation (modest response to Dll4 only), while Jagged ligands cis-inhibited both receptors. These patterns were observed in both CHO-K1 and C2C12 cells.
evaluation: Reviewers acknowledged that 'Jagged ligands have the strongest cis-inhibitory effects and the receptors differ in their sensitivity to cis-inhibition by Dll ligands' and noted these observations are 'in keeping with earlier in vivo and cell culture studies.' The qualitatively similar results in a second cell line were highlighted as evidence that findings 'reflect fundamental properties of the ligands/receptors.'

result: Trans-activation showed ultrasensitive responses with Hill coefficients ~2 (signaling activity increased approximately as the square of ligand concentration) across most ligand-receptor-Fringe combinations, while cis-inhibition showed lower ultrasensitivity (Hill coefficients ~0.75-1.5), suggesting cis-inhibition is a more stoichiometric process.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly noted that 'Responses to most trans-activating ligands showed a degree of ultrasensitivity but this was not the case for cis-interactions where effects were more linear. This has implications for the way the two mechanisms operate and for how the signaling levels will be impacted by ligand expression levels.' This was identified as a key finding.

result: Cis-inhibition strength depended on both cis-ligand and trans-ligand identity. For Notch1, each ligand preferentially cis-inhibited trans-activation by the same ligand type more efficiently than other trans-ligands. Jag2 was the most effective Notch1 cis-inhibitor overall.
evaluation: Reviewers described the work as 'the most comprehensive and rigorous analysis of the effects of canonical ligands on cis- and trans-activation, and cis-inhibition, of Notch1 and Notch2' and noted the study 'yields valuable insights.' The complexity of cis-inhibition patterns was implicitly accepted as part of the comprehensive cataloguing.

result: Lfng had opposite effects on Jag1-Notch1 binding versus activation: it increased binding strength (2.8-fold) while decreasing signaling in both coculture and plated ligand assays. This combination of strong binding with weak activation explains how Jag1 can trans-inhibit Notch1, potentially representing a core function of Jag1.
evaluation: Reviewers noted the finding that 'The failure to activate Notch1 has major functional significance' and acknowledged the data showing 'Jag1 exhibits some of the strongest binding to plate bound ligands.' The mechanistic interpretation linking binding and activation was not challenged, though reviewers noted 'it will be important in future to understanding the mechanistic basis.'

result: Lfng's effects on cis-activation resembled those on trans-activation for Notch1 (enhancing Delta, no effect on Jagged), but diverged for Notch2 (minimal effect on Delta cis-activation despite enhancing trans-activation; reducing Jag2 cis-activation >2-fold with weak trans-activation effects), suggesting cis- and trans-activation may involve different molecular mechanisms.
evaluation: Reviewers did not specifically challenge these differential Lfng effects. The overall assessment that the study 'yields valuable insights' and represents 'the most comprehensive and rigorous analysis' implicitly accepts these findings, though the mechanistic speculation was not directly evaluated.

result: Almost all ligands signaled more strongly to Notch2 than Notch1 regardless of Fringe expression (exception: Dll4 in dLfng condition). Jag2 was the strongest trans-activating ligand for both receptors with dLfng. Ligand class (Delta vs. Jagged) did not predict signaling level.
evaluation: Reviewers raised concerns about whether this reflects inherent receptor properties or differences in surface expression levels, asking 'is the fact that all ligands "signalled strongest to Notch2" an inherent property or due to differences in surface levels Notch 2 compared to Notch1?' While authors added data showing correlation between mTurquoise and surface receptor (Figure 1-supplement 1B), reviewers noted this 'goes some way to address the concerns' but did not fully resolve them.

result: Cotranslational mTurq2 reporter expression was broadly comparable between receiver clones and correlated with surface receptor expression. Ligands including Jag1 were properly trafficked to the cell surface.
evaluation: Reviewers expressed concern that 'methods used to quantify the expression of ligands and receptors rely on co-translation of tagged nuclear H2B proteins. These may not accurately capture surface levels/correctly modified transmembrane proteins.' While authors added validation data, reviewers noted 'The data analyzing surface ligand levels is more equivocal, (a Western blot for biotinylated surface proteins), as the levels detected vary substantially between Dll1 and Dll4 (the latter barely detectable).' Reviewers called for 'A discussion of the caveats of the approach.'

result: For Notch2-Dll1 and Notch2-Dll4, single-cell reporter activities correlated with cis-ligand expression regardless of preinduction culture density, ruling out the possibility that Delta-Notch2 cis-activation arises from S3-cleavage of NEXT generated by intercellular signaling during preinduction.
evaluation: Reviewers raised concerns about cis-activation physiological relevance and whether 'cells convert themselves into "signaling" and "receiving" sub-populations within the culture by post-translational mechanism.' The authors' analysis addressing this concern was not specifically challenged in the final review comments.

result: Cis- and trans-signaling combine differently across ligand-receptor combinations. For Notch1, trans-activation significantly contributed beyond cis-activation alone (especially with Lfng for Dll1/Dll4). For Notch2, only trans-Jag2 modestly increased signaling beyond cis-activation alone (~1.5-fold); other trans-ligands failed to increase signaling beyond cis-activation levels.
evaluation: Reviewers did not specifically challenge these findings about how cis and trans interactions combine. The comprehensive nature of the analysis was acknowledged, and these results fit within the overall 'cataloguing of the outcomes from the different ligand-receptor combinations.'

result: Dll1-Notch signaling was biphasic, declining at high trans-ligand expression levels. In the dLfng condition, Dll1-Notch1 signaling was only slightly above background, while Dll4 activated Notch1 9-fold more strongly than Dll1. Lfng expression reduced this difference to 2.7-fold.
evaluation: Reviewers did not challenge these specific findings about Dll1 vs Dll4 signaling differences or the biphasic response. These observations were part of the accepted comprehensive analysis of trans-activation patterns.

result: Ligands' relative cis-inhibition strengths did not correlate well with trans-activation strengths. Combinations with strong cis-activating potential (Dll4-Notch1, Dll1/Dll4-Notch2) showed poor cis-inhibition efficiency, while non-cis-activating ligands (Jag1/Jag2 for Notch1) showed strong cis-inhibition efficiency. For Notch2, no ligands favored cis-inhibition over trans-activation.
evaluation: Reviewers did not challenge these comparative analyses of cis-inhibition versus trans-activation strengths. These findings were part of the comprehensive cataloguing that reviewers acknowledged 'yields a valuable baseline for those investigating their functional roles in different contexts.'

result: CHO-K1 cells exhibit negligible endogenous Notch receptor and ligand expression with no endogenous signaling activity. Receiver cells expressed chimeric Notch receptors with intracellular domains replaced by Gal4 transcription factor.
evaluation: Reviewers did not challenge the choice or characterization of the CHO-K1 cell system. They noted the authors 'justify well their choice of players to test via this approach' and that consistency with previous publications 'provides confidence that the author's assays are working properly.'

result: Background claims about Notch pathway components, their expression patterns, canonical signaling mechanisms, and established modulatory effects including Fringe enzymes and cis/trans interactions.
evaluation: These are established background facts about the Notch pathway cited from previous literature. Reviewers did not challenge any of these foundational claims and noted that results were 'largely consistent with previous publications.'
